andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh sets 37-lakh-tonne target for 2026–27 kharif paddy procurement
facts: Civil Supplies Minister Nadendla Manohar announced a 37-lakh-metric-tonne paddy procurement target for the 2026–27 kharif season.
Procurement is scheduled to begin on 1 November 2026; this is a plan, not a report of procurement already completed.
The State plans 2,619 procurement centres and about 24,000 staff members.
The announced logistics include 31,000 vehicles and 6.10 crore gunny bags.
The government said it would seek to revise the target if production estimates warrant it.
andhraPradesh.summary: At a Vijayawada preparedness workshop, the State outlined its kharif paddy procurement target and logistics. The November start date and target are announced plans; actual procurement had not begun on 25 September.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Minimum Support Price, food procurement, agricultural marketing and the role of State civil supplies agencies.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the 37-lakh-tonne target, 2,619 centres and scheduled 1 November start; distinguish announced procurement arrangements from actual purchases.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how decentralised procurement, timely payment and transport arrangements can reduce post-harvest distress, while considering storage, fiscal and implementation constraints.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct statewide link: the target and procurement network cover Andhra Pradesh farmers and procurement centres.

andhraPradesh.headline: Nagavali and Vamsadhara floods disrupt road links in north Andhra districts
facts: Heavy rain pushed the Nagavali and Vamsadhara rivers into spate in north Andhra on 25 September.
Nagavali crossed the second warning level at Old Bridge in Srikakulam, with reported inflows of about 80,000 cusecs.
Vamsadhara crossed the first warning level at Gotta Barrage, with inflows reported at 45,679 cusecs; Bahuda inflows were reported at 35,656 cusecs.
Flooding disrupted road connectivity in Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam and Alluri Sitharama Raju districts.
District administrations issued flood alerts and mobilised rescue teams; officials reported that inflows into major reservoirs and barrages began receding by Friday evening.
andhraPradesh.summary: Rivers in north Andhra rose after several days of heavy rain, prompting alerts and response measures. Flooding also disrupted links to villages across four districts, making local access and infrastructure resilience immediate concerns.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: River systems of north Andhra, flood hazards and district-level disaster preparedness.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Locate the Nagavali and Vamsadhara systems and note the affected districts: Srikakulam, Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam and Alluri Sitharama Raju.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss the need for reliable flood warning, resilient rural road and causeway design, and coordinated response across river-basin districts.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP connection: flood alerts and disrupted road connectivity affected four Andhra Pradesh districts.

andhraPradesh.headline: Zilla Parishad administration aligned with Andhra Pradesh’s 28-district structure
facts: The State’s planned reorganisation replaces the existing 13 Zilla Praja Parishads with a structure of 28 Zilla Praja Parishads corresponding to the 28 districts.
The change takes effect after the elected bodies’ terms ended on 24 September 2026.
The arrangement maps Mandal Praja Parishads to the corresponding district-level Zilla Praja Parishads.
The government’s stated purpose is to align district-level rural local-government administration with the current district structure.
The reported reorganisation is an administrative change; it does not itself establish that fresh local-body elections have taken place.
andhraPradesh.summary: The reconstituted Zilla Parishad arrangement took effect on 25 September, matching the district-tier rural local-government structure to the State’s 28 districts. The change follows the end of the previous elected bodies’ terms; the available report describes the administrative arrangement, not completion of fresh elections.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Panchayati Raj institutions, decentralisation and district-level rural local governance under the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish Andhra Pradesh’s 28-district administrative structure from the previous 13-ZPP arrangement, and remember that ZPPs are the district tier of Panchayati Raj.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Evaluate how aligning Zilla Parishads with district boundaries may improve planning and coordination, while examining representation and continuity during transitions in elected local government.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Statewide AP governance development: the new Zilla Parishad arrangement corresponds to the State’s 28 districts.

sources.title: 28 more Zilla Parishads to come into effect in AP on Sept 25

andhraPradesh.headline: North Andhra rain replenishes reservoirs; Gambhiramgedda discharges surplus water
facts: Heavy rain associated with the weather system brought renewed inflows to reservoirs in and around Visakhapatnam district.
The New Indian Express reported Gambhiramgedda at 123 feet against a stated full reservoir level of 126 feet, with inflow of about 150 cusecs and surplus discharge downstream.
Meghadrigedda was reported at 51.50 feet against an FRL of 61 feet, with inflow of 1,578.69 cusecs.
Raiwada was reported at 341 feet against an FRL of 374 feet; Thatipudi was at 279.90 feet against an FRL of 297 feet.
The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority’s rainfall dashboard recorded state and district rainfall observations on 25 September.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: rainfall and reservoir inflows were already being tracked during the September weather event. Today: updated reporting detailed reservoir levels and discharges in Visakhapatnam district, while APSDMA continued to publish daily rainfall observations.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Andhra Pradesh drainage, reservoir management, rainfall variability and water-resource planning.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Differentiate reservoir level, full reservoir level, inflow and outflow; these are separate measures used in water monitoring.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine how intense rainfall can simultaneously improve water storage and create downstream risks, underscoring the value of real-time reservoir coordination and public warnings.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP connection: the observations concern reservoirs in Visakhapatnam district and rainfall monitoring across Andhra Pradesh.

andhraPradesh.headline: Rains damage about 690 km of roads in Andhra Pradesh; restoration estimated at ₹402 crore
facts: A Roads and Buildings Department report put rain-related damage at nearly 690 km of State roads across 13 districts.
The reported restoration estimate was ₹402.18 crore, including temporary restoration, permanent repairs and associated requirements.
Srikakulam accounted for nearly 250 km of reported road damage, the largest district share in the report.
The report listed damage to 85 cross-drainage works, with restoration underway at 62 locations.
Officials identified 614 vulnerable locations and deployed equipment and control rooms for monitoring and response.
andhraPradesh.summary: The Roads and Buildings Department’s reported assessment quantified the infrastructure impact of the rain event and estimated restoration requirements. Temporary response and restoration were reported as underway; the estimate is not evidence that permanent repairs are complete.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Road infrastructure, disaster-resilient public works and State expenditure on restoration.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The reported figure is an estimated restoration cost, not an approved or fully spent amount; distinguish temporary works from permanent repairs.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how climate-resilient road design, maintenance of cross-drainage works and transparent damage assessment can reduce the economic and social costs of extreme rainfall.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP connection: the reported damage and restoration estimate cover State Roads and Buildings Department roads across 13 AP districts.

sources.title: Rains damage 690 km roads across Andhra Pradesh, loss pegged at Rs 402 crore

andhraPradesh.headline: Agriculture Minister directs crop-loss assessment and urgent restoration after heavy rain
facts: Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu held a teleconference with senior Agriculture, Horticulture, Animal Husbandry and Fisheries officials on 25 September.
He directed officials to assess crop losses associated with persistent rain and advise farmers on preventing further damage.
Officials were also directed to assess damage to roads and other infrastructure and undertake emergency restoration.
The minister called for coordination between line departments and district administrations.
The reports describe directions to assess damage; they do not provide a completed statewide crop-loss assessment or compensation total.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: the State’s rain-response directions and district monitoring were reported on 24 September. Today: the Agriculture Minister added a department-level instruction to assess crop and infrastructure damage and coordinate emergency restoration; no completed loss assessment was reported.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Agricultural risk management, crop-loss assessment, disaster response and interdepartmental coordination.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish an instruction to assess crop losses from a completed assessment or an announced compensation package.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how rapid crop-loss verification, extension advice and coordinated restoration can protect farm livelihoods after extreme weather, while identifying the importance of timely and transparent relief processes.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Direct AP connection: the directions concern rain-affected farmers, infrastructure and district administrations in Andhra Pradesh.

national.headline: Arogya Manthan 2026 launches new digital health and PM-JAY claims initiatives
facts: Arogya Manthan 2026, organised by the National Health Authority, marked eight years of AB PM-JAY and five years of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM).
Initiatives launched included the National Healthcare Providers Registry mobile app, a Secure Data Environment and an Auto-Adjudication Framework for PM-JAY claims.
The Health Minister cited more than 60 crore PM-JAY beneficiaries and over 13 crore hospital admissions; ABDM had created over 97.8 crore ABHA accounts and linked over 121 crore health records.
Andhra Pradesh was recognised for highest PM-JAY card saturation among ASHA, Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper beneficiaries in the large-state category.
national.summary: Previous: the earlier briefing covered PM-JAY’s eighth-anniversary milestones and coverage data. Today: Arogya Manthan launched additional digital health tools, including a provider-registry app, a secure data environment and automated claims adjudication. Andhra Pradesh also received recognition for card saturation among specified frontline-worker beneficiary groups.
national.staticLink: Universal health coverage; publicly financed health insurance; digital health governance and data protection.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish AB PM-JAY, the health assurance scheme, from ABDM, the digital health ecosystem; note the three initiatives launched and Andhra Pradesh’s recognition.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how digital public infrastructure can improve claims administration and access to health services while protecting sensitive health data.
national.apLink: Andhra Pradesh was recognised in the large-state category for highest PM-JAY card saturation among ASHA, Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper beneficiaries.

national.headline: CGTMSE credit-guarantee cover goes live on three TReDS platforms
facts: The Ministry of MSME made CGTMSE credit-guarantee cover available for eligible invoice discounting on M1xchange, RXIL and DTX (KredX).
Eligibility requires both buyer and seller to be Micro or Small Enterprises; the guarantee covers 75% of the amount in default.
Maximum revolving exposure is ₹10 crore for an MSE buyer and ₹2 crore for an MSE seller.
TReDS is an RBI-regulated electronic platform for financing MSME trade receivables; the guarantee facility is intended to reduce financier risk and ease working-capital access.
national.summary: The Ministry of MSME operationalised CGTMSE-backed guarantees for eligible invoices financed through three TReDS platforms. The facility follows the Union Budget 2026–27 announcement and is intended to mitigate lender risk and help eligible Micro and Small Enterprises obtain working capital against receivables.
national.staticLink: MSME finance; credit guarantees; invoice discounting; RBI-regulated TReDS.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the three platforms, 75% guarantee coverage, and the distinct exposure limits for MSE buyers and sellers.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how credit guarantees on receivables platforms can address delayed payments and working-capital constraints for small enterprises.

sources.title: CGTMSE Guarantee Cover Goes Live on TReDS to Strengthen MSME Working Capital Access
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises

national.headline: TDB signs ₹200-crore RDI support agreement with Agnikul for reusable Agnibaan vehicle
facts: The Technology Development Board, under the Department of Science and Technology, signed an agreement with Chennai-based Agnikul Cosmos for ₹200 crore in RDI Fund support.
The project is to develop the reusable Agnibaan RLV and aims to advance the technology from Technology Readiness Level 4 or above towards TRL-8.
The programme targets a reusable launch architecture extending beyond recovery of only a launch vehicle’s first stage.
The support is to be provided through optionally convertible debentures; the project remains in development and is not an operational launch system.
national.summary: TDB signed a ₹200-crore support agreement with Agnikul Cosmos for development of its Agnibaan reusable launch vehicle. The project targets full-system reusability and technology maturation towards TRL-8; the agreement is support for development, not evidence that the vehicle is complete or operational.
national.staticLink: Indian space programme; launch vehicles; technology readiness levels; public support for research and innovation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Identify TDB as part of DST and distinguish an RDI-backed development project from a completed or operational launch vehicle.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how public risk-sharing can support private-sector innovation in strategic technologies such as reusable launch systems.

national.headline: DARPG releases August 2026 CPGRAMS reports for States and Union Territories and Central Ministries
facts: DARPG released the 49th monthly CPGRAMS report for States/UTs and the 52nd report on Central Ministries/Departments for August 2026.
States and UTs received 98,997 grievances and redressed 79,639; reported pendency stood at 2,53,040 as of 31 August 2026.
Central Ministries and Departments redressed 2,42,391 grievances in August; average grievance-disposal time in 2026 was reported as 13 days.
The central report recorded 2,51,147 grievances received and 93,864 pending; more than five lakh Common Service Centres were connected to the grievance system.
national.summary: DARPG published its August 2026 CPGRAMS performance reports for both States/UTs and Central Ministries/Departments. The releases provide grievance receipts, redressal and pendency figures, alongside central-system disposal-time and access-channel data.
national.staticLink: Citizen charters; grievance redressal; administrative accountability; e-governance.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Differentiate the State/UT report from the Central Ministries report and note their respective reporting periods and grievance statistics.
national.mainsAngle: Use grievance-redressal data to discuss responsiveness, service-delivery measurement and the limits of disposal counts as indicators of citizen satisfaction.

national.headline: NIMAS expedition completes ascents of 20 unclimbed Ladakh peaks above 6,000 metres
facts: The Defence Minister flagged in the National Institute of Mountaineering and Adventure Sports expedition on 25 September after its Ladakh mission.
A 20-member NIMAS team led by Colonel Ranveer Singh Jamwal summited 20 unclimbed peaks above 6,000 metres in 23 days.
The ascents were in the Chamser-Lungser, Gyama Nala and Chokula areas of the Ladakh Range.
The Ministry of Defence described these as the first recorded ascents of the 20 peaks.
national.summary: The NIMAS mountaineering team returned after completing ascents of 20 previously unclimbed peaks above 6,000 metres in Ladakh over 23 days. The Defence Ministry identified the climbs as first recorded ascents, and the mission concluded with the flag-in ceremony on 25 September.
national.staticLink: Himalayan physiography; high-altitude environments; mountaineering and adventure sports.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The expedition took place in the Ladakh Range, including the Chamser-Lungser, Gyama Nala and Chokula areas; the source records 20 first ascents above 6,000 metres.
national.mainsAngle: Relate high-altitude exploration to India’s frontier geography, mountaineering capacity and the need for safety and environmental safeguards.

sources.title: Raksha Mantri flags-in First Ascent Mountaineering Expedition after historic summit of 20 unclimbed peaks above 6,000 meters in Ladakh in 23 days

national.headline: NLMC concludes investor outreach for planned e-auction of 459 RINL land parcels
facts: The National Land Monetization Corporation concluded a three-city investor-outreach programme for an upcoming e-auction of 459 land parcels belonging to Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Limited (RINL).
Investor meetings were held in Visakhapatnam on 23 September, Vijayawada on 24 September and Hyderabad on 25 September 2026.
The e-auction was scheduled for October; the outreach was intended to inform prospective buyers and investors about the land portfolio and auction process.
RINL, the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, is a Navratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Steel.
national.summary: NLMC completed investor outreach ahead of the announced October e-auction of 459 RINL land parcels. Meetings in Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada give this national asset-monetisation process a direct Andhra Pradesh connection; the outreach does not mean the parcels have been sold.
national.staticLink: Public-sector asset monetisation; CPSEs; public asset management and e-auctions.
national.prelimsTakeaway: NLMC operates under the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance; RINL is the CPSE associated with Visakhapatnam Steel Plant.
national.mainsAngle: Examine the governance and public-interest considerations in monetising non-core assets of a strategic public-sector enterprise.
national.apLink: Direct AP link: RINL is the corporate entity of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, and investor meetings took place in Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada.

national.headline: Education Ministry launches Seva First Innovation Challenge for southern states and Union Territories
facts: The Education Minister inaugurated the Seva First Innovation Challenge at IISc Bengaluru and launched its website and registration portal.
The challenge invites young participants to identify community problems and develop solutions that can be tested and advanced towards implementation.
Its southern-zone coverage includes five States, including Andhra Pradesh, and three Union Territories.
Registration is open from 25 September to 24 October 2026; the national finale is scheduled for December 2026 in New Delhi.
national.summary: The Education Ministry launched the Seva First Innovation Challenge for the southern zone on 25 September. The programme is designed to connect youth-generated solutions to mentoring, incubation and possible real-world adoption; Andhra Pradesh is among the participating States.
national.staticLink: Innovation ecosystem; higher and technical education; youth participation in public problem-solving.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The challenge’s southern-zone coverage explicitly includes Andhra Pradesh; registration dates are 25 September–24 October 2026.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how student innovation programmes can link community needs, education institutions and implementation pathways.
national.apLink: Andhra Pradesh is explicitly included among the five States covered by the southern-zone challenge.

national.headline: Indian Coast Guard ship Shaunak sails for Quad-at-Sea observer mission
facts: Indian Coast Guard ship Shaunak sailed from Chennai for Perth, Australia, on 25 September for the Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission.
Six officers embarked as Sea Riders: two each from India and Japan, and one each from Australia and the United States.
The mission is intended to build maritime cooperation, interoperability and mutual trust among the four Quad countries.
The initiative was aligned with the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Joint Statement of 26 May 2026 and India’s MAHASAGAR maritime vision.
national.summary: Shaunak departed Chennai for Perth with officers from India, Japan, Australia and the United States aboard for the Quad-at-Sea observer mission. The shipboard programme is intended to strengthen professional exchanges and maritime interoperability in the Indo-Pacific.
national.staticLink: Quad; Indian Ocean and Indo-Pacific maritime cooperation; Indian Coast Guard.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The mission involves India, Australia, Japan and the United States; Shaunak sailed from Chennai to Perth with six Sea Riders.
national.mainsAngle: Assess the role of coast-guard cooperation and professional exchanges in maritime domain awareness and Indo-Pacific engagement.

national.headline: India and JICA launch workshop under forest-management capacity-enhancement project
facts: The Environment Ministry and JICA held the launch workshop for the Capacity Enhancement for Effective Forest Management Project in New Delhi.
The project’s second phase runs from FY 2025–26 to FY 2031–32 and focuses on frontline forest personnel, research and sustainable forest-management practices.
The reported project outlay is ₹537.10 crore, including a JICA contribution of ₹440.42 crore and a Government of India share of ₹96.68 crore.
The project is intended to involve States across India and address forest and wildlife management, climate concerns and field-level capacity.
national.summary: The Environment Ministry and JICA launched a workshop on 25 September for the ongoing forest-management capacity project. Its second phase is planned through FY 2031–32, with training, research and field-level capacity among its focus areas; the workshop launch does not mark completion of the project.
national.staticLink: Sustainable forest management; biodiversity conservation; climate adaptation; international development cooperation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The project is a seven-year second phase with a stated outlay of ₹537.10 crore and JICA/Union Government contributions.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how frontline capacity, local knowledge and applied research can strengthen forest governance and climate resilience.

national.headline: Minority Affairs Ministry signs institutional partnerships for monitoring, skills and entrepreneurship
facts: The Ministry of Minority Affairs signed agreements with academic and innovation institutions at IISc Bengaluru on 25 September.
IIM Bangalore was engaged for independent third-party monitoring of PM VIKAS training across the South zone.
The partnerships also involve CUBE at IIT Madras, IISc’s Foundation for Science Innovation and Development, and IIMB Innovations (NSRCEL).
The stated areas include infrastructure quality, monitoring, entrepreneurship, innovation, skilling and economic opportunities for minority communities.
national.summary: The Ministry of Minority Affairs entered into institutional agreements intended to support implementation and monitoring of its initiatives. One agreement provides for third-party monitoring of PM VIKAS training across the South zone; the agreements are partnerships, not evidence that proposed training or outcomes have already been completed.
national.staticLink: Minority welfare; skill development; public programme monitoring; social justice.
national.prelimsTakeaway: PM VIKAS training in the South zone is to receive independent third-party monitoring through IIM Bangalore.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate the role of independent monitoring and institutional partnerships in improving accountability and outcomes in targeted welfare programmes.

national.headline: MoSPI flash report tracks 1,731 Central infrastructure projects worth ₹33.60 lakh crore
facts: MoSPI’s August 2026 flash report covered 1,731 ongoing Central Sector infrastructure projects costing ₹150 crore or more.
The projects had a total revised cost of ₹33.60 lakh crore and cumulative expenditure of ₹16.33 lakh crore, about 48.59% of revised cost.
The projects were monitored across 17 Central Ministries and Departments through the PAIMANA project-monitoring platform.
The release said the next monthly flash report, for September 2026, was scheduled for 26 October 2026.
national.summary: MoSPI released its August 2026 flash report on monitored Central Sector infrastructure projects. It reported project count, revised cost and cumulative expenditure, while noting that the report covers selected categories and should be read within its stated scope.
national.staticLink: Public investment; infrastructure monitoring; project implementation and cost escalation.
national.prelimsTakeaway: PAIMANA tracked 1,731 projects with a revised cost of ₹33.60 lakh crore as of August 2026; cumulative expenditure was ₹16.33 lakh crore.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how standardised monitoring platforms can improve infrastructure accountability while recognising data coverage and implementation constraints.

international.headline: UNGA’s second pandemic-preparedness meeting renews calls for equitable global action
facts: The UN General Assembly held its second High-level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response (PPPR) in New York; the first was held in 2023.
Leaders stressed sustained and equitable investment, stronger national capacities and resilient health systems, with a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach.
The meeting highlighted One Health and equitable access to vaccines, diagnostics, therapeutics and other essential health products.

Countries called for progress on the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) annex to the WHO Pandemic Agreement; WHO said its adoption is needed before member states can begin national consideration of ratification.
The meeting did not reach consensus on the political declaration on 25 September; the UN General Assembly President said members would consider the document in future.
international.summary: The meeting renewed international commitments to pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, while underlining financing, equity and cross-border cooperation. A political declaration intended to conclude the meeting did not achieve consensus on 25 September and remains for further consideration.
international.staticLink: Global health governance; WHO; pandemic preparedness; One Health; multilateral cooperation
international.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish the WHO Pandemic Agreement from the proposed UNGA political declaration; the meeting’s declaration did not reach consensus on 25 September 2026.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how equitable financing, local health-system capacity, One Health and pathogen-sharing arrangements can strengthen global health security while addressing divides over international cooperation.

sources.title: World leaders renew commitment to protect the world from future pandemics

international.headline: G77 and China adopt 50th ministerial declaration at UN headquarters
facts: Foreign ministers of the Group of 77 and China met at UN headquarters in New York for the 50th Annual Ministerial Meeting and adopted a ministerial declaration.
The declaration reaffirmed the UN Charter, international law, multilateralism and the pursuit of a more equitable international economic order.
Ministers highlighted developing countries’ challenges across economic, social and environmental areas and called for cooperation on sustainable development.
The declaration supported equitable access to health technologies and continued international cooperation on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response.
The ministers elected Rwanda by acclamation to chair the Group of 77 for 2027.
international.summary: The ministerial declaration set out the group’s shared positions on multilateralism, development and the interests of the Global South. It also recorded Rwanda’s election as the group’s 2027 chair.
international.staticLink: Group of 77; South-South cooperation; multilateralism; global economic governance
international.prelimsTakeaway: The Group of 77 and China held its 50th Annual Ministerial Meeting on 25 September 2026; Rwanda was elected chair for 2027.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss how coalitions such as the G77 shape developing-country bargaining power in multilateral institutions, and the challenges of translating common positions into development outcomes.

sources.title: Ministerial Declaration

international.headline: WHO recommends viral composition for 2027 southern-hemisphere influenza vaccines
facts: WHO issued recommendations for the viral composition of influenza vaccines for the 2027 southern-hemisphere season after an international expert consultation.
For egg-based vaccines, WHO recommended A/Missouri/11/2025-like (H1N1)pdm09, A/Darwin/1454/2025-like (H3N2) and B/Tokyo/EIS13-175/2025-like (B/Victoria lineage) viruses.

For cell-culture, recombinant-protein or nucleic-acid-based vaccines, WHO recommended A/Missouri/11/2025-like (H1N1)pdm09, A/Darwin/1415/2025-like (H3N2) and B/Pennsylvania/14/2025-like (B/Victoria lineage) viruses.
WHO’s twice-yearly recommendations draw on surveillance through the Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) and guide vaccine development and licensing.
WHO also reviewed animal influenza viruses with human infections for pandemic preparedness.
international.summary: WHO’s recommendations provide the strain composition for vaccines intended for the 2027 southern-hemisphere influenza season. They are based on global surveillance and inform national regulators and vaccine manufacturers.
international.staticLink: Seasonal influenza; vaccine composition; global disease surveillance; zoonotic influenza
international.prelimsTakeaway: WHO issues influenza vaccine-composition recommendations twice yearly; this release covers the 2027 southern-hemisphere season.
international.mainsAngle: Explain how international disease surveillance and timely vaccine-strain selection support preparedness for seasonal and zoonotic influenza threats.

sources.title: Recommendations announced for influenza vaccine composition for the 2027 southern hemisphere influenza season

international.headline: WHO expands prequalification programme to cover contraceptives and TB-screening technology
facts: WHO announced an expansion of its medical-device prequalification programme to cover a broader range of products, including contraceptives and tuberculosis-screening technologies.
Products included in the expansion include male and female condoms, intrauterine devices, male circumcision devices and computer-aided detection software for TB screening.
The programme assesses products against international quality, safety and performance standards to inform procurement by UN agencies, donors and national authorities.

WHO said the expansion is particularly relevant to countries with limited regulatory capacity; it cited an estimated 70% of countries as having inadequate or weak regulatory systems for medicines and vaccines.
The expansion transfers prequalification for condoms and intrauterine devices from UNFPA to WHO and adds digital TB-screening technology to the programme.
international.summary: WHO broadened the scope of its prequalification programme to include additional reproductive-health devices and AI-assisted TB-screening software. The programme is intended to support procurement of quality-assured products, including in settings with weaker regulatory capacity.
international.staticLink: WHO prequalification; medical-device regulation; reproductive health; digital health; tuberculosis control

international.headline: UN Treaty Event records 36 treaty actions, including progress on cybercrime and high-seas biodiversity
facts: The UN Treaty Event concluded at UN headquarters on 25 September after running from 22 September, alongside the 81st UN General Assembly High-Level Week.
States undertook 36 treaty actions during the event, which was held under the theme “Promoting multilateral treaties – safeguarding humanity”.
The UN Convention against Cybercrime received 13 signatures during the event; the UN described it as the first global framework designed to strengthen international cooperation against cybercrime.
The BBNJ Agreement on marine biodiversity beyond national jurisdiction reached 101 ratifications during the event.
The Treaty Event provided states an opportunity to sign, ratify or accede to multilateral treaties deposited with the UN Secretary-General.
international.summary: The annual Treaty Event concluded with 36 state actions across multilateral treaties. Two notable developments were further signatures for the UN Convention against Cybercrime and the BBNJ Agreement reaching 101 ratifications.

mcqs.question: Which issue did the UN General Assembly’s second High-level Meeting on Pandemic Prevention, Preparedness and Response highlight as needing progress before member states can begin national consideration of ratification of the WHO Pandemic Agreement?
options: The Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing annex
The Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System
mcqs.explanation: The meeting called for progress on the PABS annex; WHO said its adoption is needed before national consideration of ratification can begin.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the CGTMSE credit-guarantee facility made available for eligible TReDS invoice discounting?
options: It covers 75% of the amount in default when both buyer and seller are Micro or Small Enterprises.
It covers 100% of the invoice value when either the buyer or seller is a large enterprise.
It is available only for invoices financed outside RBI-regulated platforms.
It provides a fixed guarantee of ₹10 crore to every MSE seller.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the 2026–27 kharif paddy procurement plan in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
